answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a single registered drone, listed with the aviation authority under that name. The registration, insurance, and annual inspection run roughly $220 a year, and its serial and flight log belong to that identity only. A second name needs a second drone, a second policy, and a second inspection, since one airframe cannot file two flight histories at once. A forged serial splits like light through a prism, and a copied log unravels at the first thread of telemetry. A banned drone loses its saffron tag and its registry entry.
